summary: The bill amends titles 10 and 32 of the U.S. Code to bar any order directing members of the Armed Forces or National Guard to enforce or support enforcement of immigration laws.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget allocations of any kind.
The bill does not address taxes, tax policy, or revenue measures.
No connection to healthcare policy, coverage, or markets exists in the bill text.
The legislation makes no reference to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

The bill directly amends Titles 10 and 32 to prohibit members of the Armed Forces and National Guard from enforcing or supporting enforcement of immigration laws, explicitly invoking the Posse Comitatus Act. This restricts a key federal enforcement tool at the border and for interior immigration enforcement, thereby limiting the government's capacity for stricter immigration control.
The bill has no bearing on reproductive rights or abortion access.
While the bill constrains permissible uses of the military and National Guard, it does not alter funding levels, force structure, or defense budgets.
No environmental, regulatory, or climate-related provisions are present.
The bill does not address welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety-net policies.
No education policy, school funding, or school-choice provisions appear in the text.
The legislation is silent on drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled-substance policy.

The bill reinforces the Posse Comitatus principle by barring military involvement in immigration enforcement, which has a tangential link to limits on militarized domestic policing, but the connection is narrow and indirect.
No trade, tariff, or globalization measures are included.
The bill contains no fiscal, deficit, or debt-related language.
The legislation does not address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil-rights issues.
No foreign-assistance or international-aid provisions exist.
The bill is unrelated to voting access, election administration, or voter-ID requirements.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance provisions are present.
The bill does not engage with labor law, union rights, or workplace regulations.
No religious-exemption or anti-discrimination provisions appear in the text.
